- When sentiment is consistently negative (e.g., < -0.3) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction, especially after spikes.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >50.0), model often overshoots and fails to correct — reduce forecast by 2–5% in next 3–5 periods.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 50.0 after peak), model overreacts — adjust forecast downward with smoothing factor.
- When sentiment turns positive (e.g., > 0.3) after negative streak, model often underreacts — increase forecast slightly to capture sentiment shift.
- Model underestimates true outcomes when sentiment is negative but recent price is rising — anticipate upward correction in next 2–3 periods.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overfit recent trends; apply 1–2 period lag correction — use 28-day moving average or 2-period smoothed forecast for stability.
